title.value: Can Workers Meaningfully Consent to Workplace Wellbeing Technologies?
title.justification: The title reflects the main theme of the paper, focusing on the consent and ethical implications of using wellbeing technologies in workspaces.
title.quote: Can Workers Meaningfully Consent to Workplace Wellbeing Technologies?

extractions.description: This paper explores the ethical and privacy implications of using workplace wellbeing technologies and workers' ability to meaningfully consent to them. It investigates the challenges workers face within the workplace power dynamics and suggests socio-technical interventions for supporting meaningful consent.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper revolves around consent and privacy in workplace technologies rather than any direct impact on climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: This paper unpacks challenges workers face when consenting to workplace wellbeing technologies.

primary_category.justification: Although the topic of workplace technologies is related to social and ethical concerns, it does not align with the defined list of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development categories.
primary_category.quote:
KEYWORDS
Sensing technologies deployed in the workplace can unobtrusively collect detailed data about individual activities and group interactions that are otherwise difficult to capture.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not address secondary themes directly related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
secondary_categories.quote: A hopeful application of these technologies is that they can help businesses and workers optimize productivity and wellbeing.

primary_sub_category.justification: No specific sub-category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development is applicable.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our work cuts across scholarships on quantified workplace [28, 67, 69], privacy surrounding pervasive systems [8, 47, 61], and feminist approaches to consent [34, 83, 101].

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Secondary sub-categories not tied to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development are mentioned.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The Quantified Workplace, Wellbeing Sensing, & Workplace Surveillance.

applications.justification: The paper discusses workplace wellbeing technologies, but does not focus on applications related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
applications.quote: These technologies often rely on passive sensing to enable unobtrusive collection of large-scale behavioral data in real-time and longitudinally.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on the ethical implications of consent and privacy regarding wellbeing technologies in the workplace.
new_primary_category.quote: We systematically identified both challenges to supporting meaningful consent for workplace wellbeing technologies and possible sociotechnical interventions to address them.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper specifically deals with consent mechanisms and their socio-technical aspects in the context of workplace technology.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Our work adopts FRIES as a starting point to ground a definition of meaningful consent that is sensitive to power asymmetries.
